outcome: Mother-infant bonding (measured by the Mother-to-Infant Bonding Scale)
cohort: 200 postpartum women in São José do Rio Preto, Brazil
finding: The study found that postpartum women had a high degree of bonding with their babies, which was mainly related to having had skin-to-skin contact after delivery.
mod_finding: While type of labor and pain did not significantly affect maternal bonding, lack of skin-to-skin contact was associated with lower maternal bonding scores.
